sections.content: How many people are "sports and leisure assistants"?

35,930 people

were counted on the census as "sports and leisure assistants" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Sports and leisure assistants provide and maintain facilities for sporting and recreational activities and supervise their use, maintain the continuity of entertainment and social events, offer odds and accept bets on the result of sporting and other events, control gambling activities, and work behind the scenes in production and broadcasting enterprises in a supporting role to ensure operations run smoothly.

People who had this job were generally younger

The occupation of "sports and leisure assistants" had a younger age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 20 to 24 years. Of the whole working population 7.9% were aged 20 to 24 years. For people working as "sports and leisure assistants", 24.6% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "sports and leisure assistants" was 65 years or older.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "sports and leisure assistants" included:

  • bar staff
  • waiters and waitresses
  • leisure and theme park attendants

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "sports and leisure assistants" there were more men than women (57.6% compared with 42.4%).

This means "sports and leisure assistants" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "leisure, travel and related personal service occupations".

Men made up 57.6% and women made up 42.4% of "sports and leisure assistants"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "sports and leisure assistants" included:

  • elected officers and representatives
  • ambulance staff (excluding paramedics)
  • quality assurance technicians

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "sports and leisure assistants" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "sports and leisure assistants" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "sports and leisure assistants", 10% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a younger age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (57.4% compared with 42.6%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (94%) than self-employed (6%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
